The Wave 2 gate failed on trivial compile errors, not a design problem: a missing `import os` and two wrong method calls (getInt/setInt) in SharedDataStore+Limits.swift. That is exactly the kind of thing you should fix yourself and keep going, not stop for.

Clarifying the rule for the rest of this run, and apply it going forward: the three-attempt limit means you get up to three fix-and-re-gate cycles per wave. A compile error, a missing import, a typo'd method name, a wrong signature, or any mechanical mistake in code YOU just wrote does not consume an attempt and does not trigger a stop. Just fix it and re-run the gate. Only STOP and surface to me when: a gate still fails after three genuine fix cycles, OR you would have to weaken an existing test / invariant / architecture decision to make it pass, OR you hit one of the three "must never happen" conditions. Mechanical errors in your own new code are never a reason to stop.

So: fix the import and the getInt/setInt calls now. Re-run the Wave 2 gate (three schemes sequentially + full suite + the A and C greps). If green, continue through Waves 3-6 under the clarified rule. Wave 3 still must not modify any existing planner test.

Two things to confirm while you fix: (1) the full suite was 848 tests in an earlier run and you report 789 now. Tell me why the count dropped. (2) You said the Probe folder is tracked at HEAD, not untracked as the spec assumed. Confirm you have not modified or wired it, and that the discrepancy changes nothing in your plan.

Report each wave's build result, gate status, and the A/C greps as you go. Stop only under the three conditions above.
